--- title: bc.i format: html: css: /man.css --- ## Broadcasted Integer Operations {.unnumbered} ### Description The bc.i() method performs broadcasted integer operations on 2 numeric or logical arrays.

Please note that these operations will treat the input as (53 or 32 bit) integers, and will efficiently truncate using trunc2int53() when necessary.
Therefore, something like bc.i(1, 1.5, "==") returns TRUE, because trunc(1.5) equals 1.

For regular relational operators, see [bc.rel](bc.rel.qmd).


### Usage 
bc.i(x, y, op, ...)

## S4 method for signature 'ANY'
bc.i(x, y, op)

trunc2int53(x)
### Arguments
x, y conformable vectors/arrays of type logical or numeric.
op a single string, giving the operator.
Supported integer operators: gcd, %%, %/%, pmin, pmax.
Supported relational operators: ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=.
The "gcd" operator performs the "Greatest Common Divisor" operation, using the Euclidean algorithm.
... further arguments passed to or from methods.

### Value For trunc2int53():
Base 'R' supports 53 bit integers from -1 * (2^53 - 1) to 2^53 - 1, which thus range from approximately -9 quadrillion to +9 quadrillion.
trunc2int53() will truncate a numeric vector (like trunc()), and replace all values above 2^53 - 1 with Inf, and values below -1 * (2^53 - 1) with -Inf.

For integer operators:
A numeric (double or integer, depending on the situation) array of whole numbers, as a result of the broadcasted arithmetic operation.
Values outside of the 53 bit integer range will be returned as -Inf or Inf, as in trunc2int53(), as an extra protection against integer precision loss.

For relational operators:
A logical array as a result of the broadcasted integer relational comparison.
The relational operators efficiently truncate the input during broadcasting using trunc2int53().

### References On the integer division and remainder (modulo) computations, %% and %/%:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo ### See Also [broadcast_operators](aaa01_broadcast_operators.qmd)
### Examples ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library("broadcast") x.dim <- c(4:2) x.len <- prod(x.dim) x.data <- sample(c(NA, 1.1:1000.1), x.len, TRUE) x <- array(x.data, x.dim) y <- array(1:50, c(4,1,1)) bc.i(x, y, "%%") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] 0 0 0 #> [2,] 1 0 0 #> [3,] 0 1 2 #> [4,] 3 3 0 #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] 0 0 0 #> [2,] 0 1 1 #> [3,] 2 2 1 #> [4,] 3 2 0 bc.i(x, y, "%/%") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] 897 968 684 #> [2,] 120 366 250 #> [3,] 243 57 239 #> [4,] 177 22 243 #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] 959 556 578 #> [2,] 375 459 431 #> [3,] 77 72 144 #> [4,] 86 49 206 bc.i(x, y, "gcd") # greatest common divisor #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] 1 1 1 #> [2,] 1 2 2 #> [3,] 3 1 1 #> [4,] 1 1 4 #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] 1 1 1 #> [2,] 2 1 1 #> [3,] 1 1 1 #> [4,] 1 2 4 bc.i(x, y, "==") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE bc.i(x, y, "!=") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE bc.i(x, y, "<") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE bc.i(x, y, ">") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE bc.i(x, y, "<=") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [2,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [3,] FALSE FALSE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE FALSE FALSE bc.i(x, y, ">=") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE ``` :::
